system.description:
You have been taught that faith requires more than prayer. There are things that hide behind scripture, wear familiar faces and speak sacred words while corrupting everything those words were meant to protect. Possessing spirits whisper through unwilling mouths. Necromancers bind souls that should have passed beyond mortal reach. False prophets manufacture miracles. Cursed relics lie beneath temple altars, and sometimes the greatest threat to a faith is found within its own hierarchy.
You are trained to find these things.
Grimwards are investigators, interrogators and hunters employed by temples, sacred orders and independent religious authorities to uncover supernatural corruption. Some are solemn exorcists who would rather save a possessed victim than destroy them. Others are relentless witch-hunters, doctrinal investigators or wandering judges who believe that no institution - including their own - is above examination.
You combine practical investigative training with limited Divinity magic and enough martial skill to survive when an inquiry becomes violent. You are not a Crusader. A Crusader stands openly before an enemy and challenges them through strength, conviction and divine favour. You watch first. You ask questions. You examine the body, read the ward, speak to the witnesses, identify the thing wearing the priest's face - and only then do you draw your weapon.
Your greatest strength is Inquisition. By concentrating upon a particular creature, you can gather information, identify patterns and eventually place that creature under Judgement. Once you understand your enemy, you become considerably more dangerous to them.
You may want to play a Grimward if you enjoy investigation, monster hunting, interrogation, limited divine magic and turning knowledge about a specific enemy into combat advantage.
A Grimward does not burn someone because they are accused of heresy. A competent Grimward first determines whether there was ever any heresy at all.

MAGICAL TRADITION
You are an instinctive Divinity spellcaster. Your magical training is less extensive than that of a Cleric, but Grimwards are deliberately taught a broad range of practical divine magic. An investigation may require protection from a curse one day, healing the victim of a possession the next, and destroying the creature responsible on the third. Grimward training therefore values adaptability over specialisation.
At 1st level, select any two PP 2 spells from the Divinity tradition and add them to your spell repertoire.
At 2nd level and every level thereafter, you may select one additional Divinity spell that you are capable of casting and add it to your repertoire.
You may cast these spells whenever you meet their casting requirements and do not need to memorise them.
At 5th level and every two levels thereafter, you may replace one spell in your Grimward repertoire with another eligible Divinity spell.
Spells granted by your Divine Aspect are added to your repertoire automatically and do not count against the number of Grimward spells you know.

SPECIALIST SPELLS
At 1st level, you gain one PP 1 Specialist Spell granted by your Divine Aspect. You may learn additional Grimward Specialist Spells through class feats presented in Chapter 5.
system.classSkills: Athletics, Culture, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Linguistics, Medicine, Mental Focus, Occultism, Perception, Religion, Sense Motive, Stealth, Survival
system.classAbilities: 1: Inquisition, 1: Judgement, 1: Reconstruct Target, 1: Prepared Adversary, 1: Deific Aspect (Grimward), 1: Inquisitorial Discipline, 2: Grim Resolve, 4: Sanctioned Strike
system.proficiencies: You are proficient in light and medium armour and shields, except tower shields. You are proficient with all simple and martial weapons.

trg-prime.bonusFeatsNote: At 1st level, you gain one bonus class feat. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you gain an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or possess the appropriate Grimward, Expert or Adept trait for the feat.
